q.t: A toy is bought for ₹200 and sold for ₹250. Find the profit (in ₹).
q.e: Profit = selling price − cost price = 250 − 200 = 50. You got back more than you paid.

q.t: A book is bought for ₹500 and sold for ₹450. Find the loss (in ₹).
q.e: Loss = cost price − selling price = 500 − 450 = 50. You got back less than you paid.

q.t: A shopkeeper makes a profit when:
q.e: Profit means money gained — the selling price (SP) must be higher than the cost price (CP).

q.t: CP = ₹100 and SP = ₹120. Find the profit percent.
q.e: Profit = 20. Profit % = profit/CP × 100 = 20/100 × 100 = 20%.

q.t: CP = ₹400 and the loss is ₹40. Find the SP (in ₹).
q.e: With a loss, SP = CP − loss = 400 − 40 = 360.

q.t: SP = ₹660 and the profit is ₹60. Find the CP (in ₹).
q.e: SP = CP + profit, so CP = 660 − 60 = 600.

q.t: An article is bought for ₹50 and sold for ₹50. The seller has:
q.e: SP = CP, so nothing is gained or lost.

q.t: Profit percent and loss percent are always calculated on the:
q.e: The cost price is the money you put in, so gain or loss is compared with it.

q.t: CP = ₹800 and the profit is 10%. Find the profit (in ₹).
q.e: 10% of the cost price: 800 ÷ 10 = 80.

q.t: CP = ₹250 and SP = ₹200. Find the loss percent.
CP = ₹1200 and the gain is 15%. Find the SP (in ₹).
SP = ₹540 and the loss is 10%. Find the CP (in ₹).
q.e: A 10% loss means SP is 90% of CP. 90% → 540, so 100% → 600.

q.t: A table is bought for ₹750. ₹50 is spent on transport, and it is sold for ₹920. Find the gain percent.
q.e: Overheads are part of the cost: total CP = 800. Gain = 120. 120/800 × 100 = 15%.

q.t: SP = ₹1680 and the gain is 12%. Find the CP (in ₹).
CP = ₹640 and SP = ₹560. Find the loss percent.
12 pens are bought for ₹60 and sold at ₹6 each. Find the profit percent.
q.e: SP of 12 pens = 72. Profit = 12 on a cost of 60: 12/60 × 100 = 20%.

q.t: CP = ₹2400 and the loss is 8%. Find the SP (in ₹).
An article costing ₹950 is sold at a gain of 20%. Find the gain (in ₹).
q.e: 20% of 950 = one fifth of 950 = 190.

q.t: 20 kg of rice is bought at ₹45 per kg and all of it is sold for ₹1080. Find the gain percent.
SP = ₹931 and the loss is 5%. Find the CP (in ₹).
The cost price of 10 articles equals the selling price of 8 articles. Find the gain percent.
q.e: Let each cost ₹1. Then 8 articles (cost ₹8) sell for ₹10: gain 2 on 8 = 25%.

q.t: A man buys 6 dozen eggs at ₹60 a dozen. 12 eggs break, and he sells the rest at ₹7 each. Find his gain percent.
Selling a chair for ₹720 gives a gain of 20%. At what price should it be sold to gain 35% (in ₹)?
q.e: First find the CP: 720 ÷ 1.2 = 600. Then 135% of 600 = 810.

q.t: Selling a fan for ₹450 gives a loss of 10%. At what price should it be sold to gain 10% (in ₹)?
A toy is bought for ₹80 and ₹20 is spent on repairs. It is sold at a profit of 25%. Find the SP (in ₹).
q.e: Total cost = 100. 25% profit on 100 gives SP = 125.

q.t: A man buys 100 oranges for ₹400. He sells 60 of them at ₹5 each and the other 40 at ₹4 each. Find his gain percent.
A cycle is sold for ₹1955 at a gain of 15%. Find its CP (in ₹).
A trader gains an amount equal to 1/5 of the cost price. What is his gain percent?
q.e: Gain/CP = 1/5, and 1/5 as a percentage is 20%.

q.t: By selling 45 m of cloth, a shopkeeper gains the selling price of 5 m. Find his gain percent.
q.e: Let SP be ₹1 per metre: SP = 45, gain = 5, so CP = 40. Gain % = 5/40 × 100 = 12.5% — on CP, not SP.

q.t: A radio sold for ₹564 gives a loss of 6%. What would the gain percent be if it were sold for ₹648?
q.e: 564 is 94% of CP, so CP = 600. Selling at 648 gains 48: 48/600 = 8%.

q.t: Two radios are sold for ₹990 each. On one there is a gain of 10% and on the other a loss of 10%. Overall the seller has:
q.e: CPs: 990 ÷ 1.1 = 900 and 990 ÷ 0.9 = 1100, total 2000. Total SP = 1980. Loss 20 on 2000 = 1%. The 10% loss was on the bigger amount.

q.t: Toffees are bought at 11 for ₹10 and sold at 10 for ₹11. Find the gain percent.
q.e: Take 110 toffees: cost = 10 lots of 11 → ₹100; sale = 11 lots of 10 → ₹121. Gain 21 on 100 = 21%.

q.t: A sells a bicycle to B at a profit of 20%. B sells it to C at a profit of 25%. C pays ₹1500. What did A pay for it (in ₹)?
q.e: Work backwards: B paid 1500 ÷ 1.25 = 1200. A paid 1200 ÷ 1.2 = 1000.

q.t: A man sells an article at a loss of 5%. If he had sold it for ₹60 more, he would have gained 7%. Find the CP (in ₹).
q.e: From 5% loss to 7% gain is a swing of 12% of CP, and that equals ₹60. CP = 60 ÷ 0.12 = 500.

q.t: Lemons are bought at 4 for ₹10 and sold at 3 for ₹10. Find the gain percent.
q.e: Take 12 lemons: cost = ₹30, sale = ₹40. Gain 10 on 30 = 1/3 = 33 1/3%.

q.t: A grocer mixes 30 kg of rice costing ₹40 per kg with 20 kg costing ₹50 per kg and sells the mixture at ₹55 per kg. Find his gain percent.
The profit made by selling a bag for ₹850 equals the loss made by selling it for ₹650. Find its CP (in ₹).
q.e: 850 − CP = CP − 650, so the CP is exactly halfway: (850 + 650) ÷ 2 = 750.

q.t: A watch is sold at a loss of 12%. Had it been sold for ₹140 more, there would have been a gain of 8%. Find the CP (in ₹).
q.e: From −12% to +8% is 20% of CP = 140, so CP = 700.

q.t: A trader buys 200 kg of fruit at ₹30 per kg. 10% of it spoils and he sells the rest at ₹40 per kg. Find his gain percent.
q.e: CP = 6000 (he paid for all 200 kg). He sells 180 kg for 7200. Gain 1200 on 6000 = 20%.

q.t: Goods costing ₹1200 are sold in two lots: one-third of them at a profit of 15% and the rest at a loss of 6%. Overall the trader has:
q.e: One-third costs 400 → sold for 460. The rest costs 800 → sold for 752. Total SP = 1212, a gain of 12 on 1200 = 1%.
